model.name: Software Product
model.purpose: Describe a software product in full context so an agent can identify it, know what it is made of, what rights and obligations attach to it, where it actually runs, how long it is supported, and what evidence backs every claim.
model.scope_statement: This model is the host aggregate for software regarded simultaneously as a published offering (product line, releases, distributable artifacts, licences) and as an operated system (deployed instances, environments, effective configuration, advisories). It is an aggregate rather than a plain entity because release, deployment and advisory records have independent lifecycles yet are only meaningful when anchored to one product identity. It is format-neutral: SPDX, CycloneDX, CSAF, JSON, Git, MongoDB and MCP are projections of these findings, not their semantics. Component-internal and package-ecosystem detail is delegated to WM-SFT-007 by COMPOSE and is not restated here.
in_scope: Product identity, classification, producer accountability and identifier coordinates (purl, CPE, SWID, content identifiers)
Release lineage: version strings, versioning scheme, publication events, channels, withdrawal and supersession
Product-level composition: the bill of materials document, declared dependency constraints and their recorded resolution
Build provenance, artifact integrity, signatures and secure-development assurance claims
Licence declaration, third-party attribution obligations, use and export restrictions
Deployed instances, hosting environments, effective configuration and exposed interfaces
Support lifecycle, end-of-life milestones, update delivery, advisories and exploitability assessment
Quality characteristics, verification evidence and regulatory conformity documentation
out_of_scope: Internal structure, ecosystem metadata and package-manager semantics of individual components and packages (WM-SFT-007)
Organization records for producers, suppliers and operators beyond a reference to them
Rights-holder, patent and trademark records as subject matter in their own right
Dataset and AI training-corpus records consumed or produced by the software
Source-control history, issue tracking, requirements engineering and project management processes
Vulnerability records themselves as governed objects (CVE/CWE registry content), as opposed to this product's exposure to them
Hardware devices and physical assets except as the hosting platform of a deployed instance
Commercial contracts, pricing and entitlement fulfilment mechanics

boundary_notes.distinction: This model records that a release is composed of components and the resolution that satisfied each declared dependency; it does not model a component's own identity, ecosystem metadata or internal files. SPDX distinguishes the Sbom/Bom collection from the Package and File elements it contains, and CycloneDX separates the BOM document from the component objects; the seam is drawn at that same line.

SPDX models Agent, Person and Organization as first-class elements referenced by artifacts. This model holds only the reference plus the role that party plays for this product; legal identity, addresses and corporate hierarchy belong to the organization model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Vulnerability registry (CVE Program) and advisory publishers
boundary_notes.distinction: CVE records and CVSS scores are governed by the CVE Program and its record format. This model stores the exposure mapping and the product's exploitability assessment, referencing the CVE identifier rather than restating the vulnerability record.
The licence expression, copyright holder reference and obligation classes attached to a release are in scope; the underlying rights instruments, assignments and disputes are not.

purl types, CPE dictionary governance and SWID tag-issuer rules are governed elsewhere. This model records which coordinates denote this product and how conflicts between schemes are resolved for a given use.

CycloneDX separates components from services and supports a SaaSBOM. Where software is delivered only as a hosted service with no distributable artifact, the release and integrity layers degrade to service-version records; that degradation is recorded explicitly rather than by forcing artifact semantics.

ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 defines processes for acquiring, supplying, developing, operating, maintaining and disposing of software. This model describes the product and system as objects with states and evidence; it does not define or govern the processes themselves.

findings.name: Product Identity Record
findings.description: The authoritative record that fixes the product's master-system identifier, canonical name, issuing namespace, producer of record and the criterion separating it from adjacent offerings.

data_elements.name: Product master key
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier for the product issued by the producer's system of record, stored with the issuing system so its authority is auditable.

data_elements.name: Canonical product name
data_elements.description: The name under which the product is offered, as published by the producer.

data_elements.name: Producer reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the organization record for the producing or supplying party, not an embedded copy of it.

data_elements.name: Identity namespace
data_elements.description: Namespace or registry in which the canonical name and master key are unique.

data_elements.name: Alternate names
data_elements.description: Marketing, legacy and internal names that alias the canonical name, each with the context in which it is used.

findings.name: Identifier Coordinates and Crosswalk
findings.description: Ecosystem-facing coordinates that let external systems match this product and its releases (Package URL, CPE, SWID, download location, content identifiers), plus the mapping and precedence between them.

data_elements.name: Package URL
data_elements.description: Canonical purl identifying the distributed package form, per the governed syntax.

data_elements.name: CPE name
data_elements.description: Formatted CPE string asserted to denote this product for vulnerability applicability matching.

data_elements.name: Content identifier
data_elements.description: Content-derived identifier for a specific artifact, such as a source or artifact content hash identifier.

data_elements.name: Coordinate assertion
data_elements.description: Who asserted a coordinate, when, and on what evidence; separates producer declaration from third-party attribution.

findings.name: Family, edition, channel and SKU
findings.description: CoSWID software-meta separates product, product-family, edition, channel-type, colloquial-version and revision from the exact software-version. CSAF product trees use vendor/product/version branches, product groups and relationships among products. These group commercial variants (enterprise versus standard, OEM versus academic, LTS line) without treating each SKU as an unrelated product or collapsing them into a single version.

data_elements.name: Product family
data_elements.description: Family spanning client, server or related capabilities

data_elements.name: Edition
data_elements.description: Functional variation such as standard or enterprise

data_elements.name: Channel type
data_elements.description: Sales or licensing channel such as OEM, retail, academic or volume

data_elements.name: Colloquial version
data_elements.description: Informal line label such as a year or major train

data_elements.name: Product group identifier
data_elements.description: CSAF product group id when variants are grouped for advisory status

findings.name: Software Classification and Purpose
findings.description: Controlled typing of the software (component type, primary and additional purpose, delivery model, regulatory class) that determines which downstream profiles and obligations apply.

data_elements.name: Component type code
data_elements.description: Type drawn from a declared controlled vocabulary such as application, library, framework, container, operating-system, firmware, device-driver, machine-learning-model.

data_elements.name: Primary purpose code
data_elements.description: Declared primary purpose of the artifact, with any additional purposes recorded separately.

data_elements.name: Delivery model code
data_elements.description: How the product reaches the consumer: downloadable artifact, image, embedded firmware, or hosted service.

data_elements.name: Regulatory class
data_elements.description: Class assigned under a named product-security or market regime, with the regime reference.

findings.name: Producer Accountability and Record Stewardship
findings.description: The split of ownership and authority over the record: producer-side release facts versus operator-side deployment facts, who may publish binding statements, and what happens when stewardship lapses.

data_elements.name: Steward assignment
data_elements.description: Binding of a record slice to an owning role and owner package, with validity window.

data_elements.name: Authority delegation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the delegation that entitles a party to publish binding statements about the product.

data_elements.name: Record author reference
data_elements.description: The party that authored a given record or document, kept distinct from the producer reference.

data_elements.name: Stewardship succession rule
data_elements.description: Declared rule for reassigning stewardship on acquisition, dissolution or abandonment.

findings.name: Release Record
findings.description: One published version of the product: its version string, publication event time and observation time, distribution channel, state and supersession links.

data_elements.name: Version string
data_elements.description: The producer's exact version label for the release, stored verbatim alongside a derived ordering key.

data_elements.name: Publication event time
data_elements.description: The time the release was made available, recorded as an RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit offset.

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: The time this record observed or ingested the release fact, held separately from publication time.

data_elements.name: Release state
data_elements.description: Current lifecycle state of the release within the producer's publication process.

data_elements.name: Supersession reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the release this one replaces, and to any release that replaces it.

findings.name: Version Scheme and Ordering
findings.description: The declared versioning scheme and precedence rules that make version comparison, dependency ranges and affected-range statements decidable rather than guessed.

data_elements.name: Version scheme
data_elements.description: Identifier of the versioning scheme in force, such as a semantic scheme, a calendar scheme or an ecosystem-specific scheme.

data_elements.name: Ordering key
data_elements.description: Derived comparable key used for range evaluation, computed by the declared scheme and recomputed when the scheme changes.

data_elements.name: Compatibility promise
data_elements.description: Stated contract about what consumers may rely on across increments of each version component.

findings.name: Patch versus upgrade and tag types
findings.description: CoSWID and NISTIR 8060 define four tag types used at different lifecycle points: corpus (pre-install media), primary (installed component), patch (incremental fix that MUST NOT change software-version) and supplemental (site-added metadata). Patch tags MUST link with rel=patches to the patched software. Upgrade replaces primary tags and changes version metadata. This distinction is a frequent omission in product catalogues that only store version strings.

data_elements.name: Tag type
data_elements.description: corpus, primary, patch or supplemental

data_elements.name: Patched release reference
data_elements.description: Release this patch applies to

data_elements.name: Patch changes version flag
data_elements.description: Must be false for a CoSWID patch tag

data_elements.name: Corpus installation media
data_elements.description: Pre-install package or installer location

findings.name: Distribution Channel and Availability
findings.description: Authoritative download locations and registries for a release, the access conditions attached to them, and how long prior releases stay retrievable.

data_elements.name: Download location
data_elements.description: Resolvable location from which the distributable artifact may be obtained, flagged as authoritative or mirror.

data_elements.name: Distribution condition
data_elements.description: Condition governing who may obtain the release from the location.

data_elements.name: Distribution retention period
data_elements.description: Declared period for which the release remains retrievable at the distribution point.

findings.name: Artifact Integrity and Signature
findings.description: Hashes, signatures and signing identities that let a consumer verify a fetched artifact, together with the verification outcome and any reproducibility claim.

data_elements.name: Hash entry
data_elements.description: Algorithm plus lowercase hexadecimal digest for a named distributable artifact.

data_elements.name: Signature block
data_elements.description: Detached or embedded signature over the artifact or its digest, with the signature scheme identified.

data_elements.name: Signing identity reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the key, certificate or workload identity that produced the signature.

data_elements.name: Verification outcome
data_elements.description: Result of a verification attempt, with verifier identity and observation time.

findings.name: Bill of Materials Document
findings.description: The SBOM treated as a dated, authored document about one release: its format and specification version, author, creation time, declared depth and explicitly declared known unknowns.

data_elements.name: BOM format
data_elements.description: Named bill-of-materials format used for the document.

data_elements.name: BOM specification version
data_elements.description: Exact specification version the document claims to conform to.

data_elements.name: BOM creation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and offset recording when the document was generated, distinct from the release publication time.

data_elements.name: Declared depth
data_elements.description: The claimed traversal depth of the composition described.

data_elements.name: Known unknown entry
data_elements.description: Explicit declaration that a portion of the composition could not be determined, with reason.

findings.name: Dependency Graph and Resolution
findings.description: Declared dependency constraints with scope and optionality, the concrete releases that satisfied them at build time, and the pinning that makes the resolution reproducible.

data_elements.name: Dependency declaration
data_elements.description: A declared need on another component expressed as a constraint range with scope and optionality.

data_elements.name: Resolved component reference
data_elements.description: Reference into the component and package model for the release that actually satisfied a declared constraint.

data_elements.name: Dependency scope
data_elements.description: Whether the dependency is required, optional or excluded at the stated stage such as build, runtime or test.

data_elements.name: Resolution lock digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the pinned resolution set that makes a rebuild verifiable.

findings.name: Coverage, completeness and known unknowns
findings.description: CISA 2026 replaces NTIA Depth with Coverage (horizontal and vertical breadth) and requires explicitly identifying unknown information. CycloneDX compositions aggregate completeness as complete, incomplete, incomplete first-party only, incomplete third-party only or unknown. SPDX Sbom may carry multiple sbomTypes. An SBOM that omits unknowns is less operable than one that marks them. Completeness is a quality measurement of the composition evidence, not of the software.

data_elements.name: Coverage statement
data_elements.description: Horizontal and vertical coverage claimed

data_elements.name: Completeness aggregate
data_elements.description: CycloneDX composition aggregate value

data_elements.name: Known unknowns
data_elements.description: Explicit unknown component, license or dependency slots

data_elements.name: First-party completeness
data_elements.description: Whether first-party content is complete

data_elements.name: Third-party completeness
data_elements.description: Whether third-party content is complete

findings.name: Build Provenance Attestation
findings.description: Machine-verifiable provenance identifying the build platform and builder, the top-level inputs and source revision, the parameters used, and the build-integrity level the provenance supports.

data_elements.name: Builder identity
data_elements.description: Identity of the entity that executed the build, as asserted in the provenance.

data_elements.name: Source revision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the exact source revision consumed by the build, held as a reference to the source-control model.

data_elements.name: Provenance predicate type
data_elements.description: The attestation predicate type and version, so consumers know how to interpret the payload.

data_elements.name: Build assurance level
data_elements.description: Claimed build track level, recorded with whether it is self-claimed or independently verified.

findings.name: Secure Development Practice Assurance
findings.description: Claims about the producer's secure development practices, the evidence for each claim, and whether the claim is self-attested, customer-audited or third-party assessed.

data_elements.name: Practice claim
data_elements.description: A single claimed practice with its framework identifier and scope.

data_elements.name: Attestation type
data_elements.description: Basis of the claim: self-attestation, customer audit or third-party assessment.

data_elements.name: Assessor reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party that assessed or audited the claim, where not self-attested.

findings.name: Licence Declaration and Expression
findings.description: The licence expression applying to a release, distinguishing what the producer declared from what an analyst concluded, with the copyright holder and any licence change across releases.

data_elements.name: Licence expression
data_elements.description: Governed licence expression for the release, using a declared expression syntax and identifier list.

data_elements.name: Determination basis
data_elements.description: Whether the expression is declared by the producer or concluded by analysis, with the determining party.

data_elements.name: Copyright text
data_elements.description: Copyright statement as published with the artifact.

data_elements.name: Copyright holder reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the rights-holder record in the intellectual property model.

findings.name: Third-Party Attribution Obligations
findings.description: Obligations inherited from bundled third-party components: attribution notices that must ship, reciprocal obligations and their reach, and corresponding-source availability duties with their duration.

data_elements.name: Attribution notice entry
data_elements.description: A single notice that must be reproduced, bound to the component that requires it.

data_elements.name: Obligation class
data_elements.description: Classification of the obligation such as notice-only, reciprocal or source-availability.

data_elements.name: Corresponding source location
data_elements.description: Where corresponding source is offered, with the period for which the offer stands.

findings.name: Use and Export Restrictions
findings.description: Restrictions on who may obtain, run or re-export the product, including entitlement requirements, field-of-use exclusions, jurisdictional controls and documented waivers.

data_elements.name: Entitlement requirement
data_elements.description: What a recipient must hold to obtain or run the release.

data_elements.name: Field-of-use exclusion
data_elements.description: A deployment context excluded by licence, contract or regulation.

data_elements.name: Export classification
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction-specific export control classification with the determining party.

data_elements.name: Waiver record
data_elements.description: Documented exception to a restriction, with approver and validity window.

findings.name: Deployed Instance Record
findings.description: One running installation of a specific release: its operator-side identifier, the version observed running, the window over which it ran, its purpose and its criticality.

data_elements.name: Instance key
data_elements.description: Operator's authoritative identifier for the deployed instance.

data_elements.name: Running release reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the release observed running on the instance.

data_elements.name: Deployment observation time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and offset for when the running state was observed, distinct from the go-live event time.

data_elements.name: Deployment window
data_elements.description: Interval over which the instance ran the referenced release, bounded by go-live and change events.

data_elements.name: Criticality level
data_elements.description: Operator's assessment of the instance's business criticality, used to prioritise advisory response.

findings.name: Hosting Environment and Platform
findings.description: The environment class, platform stack, jurisdictional location and network exposure of the host on which instances run.

data_elements.name: Environment class
data_elements.description: Class of the hosting environment within the operator's promotion model.

data_elements.name: Platform descriptor
data_elements.description: Operating system, runtime and image identification for the hosting stack, referencing component records rather than restating them.

data_elements.name: Hosting location
data_elements.description: Region and jurisdiction in which the instance is hosted.

data_elements.name: Network exposure
data_elements.description: Whether and how the instance is reachable from untrusted networks.

findings.name: Effective Configuration State
findings.description: The configuration actually in effect on an instance, its deviation from the released default or hardened baseline, and the change events that produced it. This matters because exploitability assessments are frequently conditional on configuration.

data_elements.name: Configuration item
data_elements.description: A single security-relevant configuration key and its effective value, with collection method.

data_elements.name: Baseline deviation
data_elements.description: Difference between an effective value and its baseline value, with an annotation of consequence.

data_elements.name: Configuration change event
data_elements.description: Recorded change to configuration with actor, authorisation and RFC 3339 event time.

findings.name: External Interfaces and Data Flows
findings.description: Services, endpoints and data flows a deployed instance exposes or consumes, including third-party services that are dependencies but never shipped as components.

data_elements.name: Interface descriptor
data_elements.description: An exposed or consumed endpoint with protocol, direction and trust boundary crossed.

data_elements.name: Service dependency reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an external service the instance depends on, modelled as a service rather than a component.

data_elements.name: Data category
data_elements.description: Category of data crossing an interface, flagged where it is personal or regulated.

findings.name: Support Status and End of Life
findings.description: The producer's binding statement about how long a product line or release receives fixes, the dated milestones that end that obligation, and what happens to instances that outlive it.

data_elements.name: Support status
data_elements.description: Current support state of a release line such as full support, maintenance only, security fixes only, or ended.

data_elements.name: End-of-support date
data_elements.description: Announced date after which fixes cease, stored as a date and never used as an identifier.

data_elements.name: Lifecycle announcement event
data_elements.description: The announcement that set or changed a lifecycle milestone, with RFC 3339 event time and publisher.

data_elements.name: Declared support period
data_elements.description: Length of the committed support period for the product, used to test against regulatory minimums.

findings.name: Update and Patch Delivery
findings.description: How fixes reach deployed instances: channels, mechanism, default automation, separability of security fixes from feature change, and evidence that an update was actually applied.

data_elements.name: Update channel
data_elements.description: Named channel through which updates are published to consumers.

data_elements.name: Automatic update default
data_elements.description: Whether updates are applied automatically unless the operator opts out.

data_elements.name: Update application record
data_elements.description: Evidence that a specific instance applied a specific update, with actor and RFC 3339 event time.

findings.name: Advisory and Exposure Mapping
findings.description: Notices of defects or vulnerabilities and the mapping from each notice to affected version ranges, contained components and deployed instances, with severity and any authority-reporting duty.

data_elements.name: Advisory identifier
data_elements.description: Publisher-issued advisory identifier with its tracking version and current release time.

data_elements.name: Vulnerability identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the governed vulnerability record, not a copy of it.

data_elements.name: Affected version range
data_elements.description: Version range declared affected, with the range expression syntax and default status.

data_elements.name: Severity score
data_elements.description: Asserted score with vector, scoring system version and asserting party.

data_elements.name: Advisory publication time
data_elements.description: Initial and current release times of the advisory, recorded as RFC 3339 date-times with seconds and offset.

findings.name: Exploitability Assessment
findings.description: The product-specific determination of whether a vulnerability present in a contained component is actually exploitable in this product or deployment, with a recognised justification and its conditions.

data_elements.name: Exploitability status
data_elements.description: Product status for a specific vulnerability, drawn from the governing exchange vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Justification code
data_elements.description: Recognised reason for a not-affected status, from the governing vocabulary rather than free text.

data_elements.name: Applicability condition
data_elements.description: Configuration or environment conditions under which the assessment holds.

data_elements.name: Assessment revision
data_elements.description: Revision number and time of the assessment, with the superseded statement retained.

findings.name: Remediation, entitlements and restart
findings.description: CSAF remediations carry category, date, details, product or group ids, URL, restart-required and entitlements. Entitlements here are access gates on a remediation (who may obtain the fix), not the intellectual-property license of the software. CoSWID activation-status and entitlement-key similarly record install-time activation without storing unprotected license secrets. Restart-required is an operational constraint on deployed systems.

data_elements.name: Remediation category
data_elements.description: vendor_fix, workaround, mitigation, none_available or no_fix_planned

data_elements.name: Remediation URL
data_elements.description: Locator of the fix or guidance

data_elements.name: Restart required
data_elements.description: Whether and how a restart is required

data_elements.name: Remediation entitlements
data_elements.description: Who is entitled to obtain the fix

data_elements.name: Activation status
data_elements.description: trial, licensed, unlicensed or similar CoSWID activation-status

findings.name: Quality Characteristics and Measures
findings.description: The quality characteristics selected for this product from a governed quality model, the measure and target defined for each, and the values actually measured on a named release.

data_elements.name: Quality characteristic
data_elements.description: Characteristic or subcharacteristic selected from the declared quality model.

data_elements.name: Quality measure
data_elements.description: Definition of the measure and method used to evaluate a characteristic.

data_elements.name: Target value
data_elements.description: Target or acceptance threshold for a measure, with unit.

data_elements.name: Measured value
data_elements.description: Observed value for a measure on a named release, with measurement time and conditions.

findings.name: Verification and Test Evidence
findings.description: Evidence that a release was verified: which activities were performed, how each result binds to the exact artifact digest tested, and which defects were knowingly accepted at release.

data_elements.name: Verification activity
data_elements.description: A performed verification activity with its type, scope and performing party.

data_elements.name: Evidence subject digest
data_elements.description: Digest of the artifact the evidence describes, binding evidence to a specific build.

data_elements.name: Accepted defect
data_elements.description: Known open defect accepted at release, with accepting party and rationale.

findings.name: Conformity Assessment and Technical Documentation
findings.description: The regulatory regimes in scope for placing the product on each target market, the conformity assessment route used, the declaration or marking issued, and the technical documentation with its retention duty.

data_elements.name: Regulatory regime reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an applicable product-regulation regime and the market it governs.

data_elements.name: Conformity assessment route
data_elements.description: The assessment procedure used, including whether a third party was involved.

data_elements.name: Declaration of conformity reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the issued declaration and the exact releases it covers.

data_elements.name: Documentation retention period
data_elements.description: Period for which technical documentation must be kept available to authorities.

functions.name: Register software product
functions.description: Create the product identity record, binding a master-system identifier, namespace, canonical name and producer reference before any release, licence or deployment statement may attach to it.

functions.name: Publish release
functions.description: Record a published version of the product with its publication event time, observation time, channel, state and at least one integrity value.

functions.name: Attach bill of materials
functions.description: Associate a versioned, authored bill-of-materials document with a specific release, recording format, specification version, author, creation time, declared depth and known unknowns.

functions.name: Verify artifact integrity
functions.description: Check a fetched artifact against its published digests, signatures and provenance attestation, and record the verification outcome with the verifier identity and time.

functions.name: Resolve dependency set
functions.description: Evaluate declared dependency constraints against available component releases, record the concrete resolution with resolver identity and lock digest, and preserve the build-time resolution distinctly from any later re-resolution.

functions.name: Record deployment observation
functions.description: Record that a specific instance was observed running a specific release in a specific environment, with the observation method and time kept separate from the go-live event time.

functions.name: Assess vulnerability exposure
functions.description: Map an advisory to affected releases through the bill of materials, then to deployed instances, then record a product-specific exploitability status with a recognised justification and its applicability conditions.

functions.name: Declare end of support
functions.description: Publish or revise a lifecycle statement setting support status and end-of-support or end-of-life milestones for a product or release line, and test the declared period against applicable regulatory minimums.

functions.name: Compile conformity dossier
functions.description: Assemble the technical documentation required by an applicable market regime from identity, composition, provenance, verification, licensing and lifecycle findings, and place it under the regime's retention duty.

functions.name: Revise identification tag
functions.description: Increment tag-version to correct metadata without changing software-version.

functions.name: Apply patch tag
functions.description: Install a patch tag linked with rel=patches that must not change software-version, or perform an upgrade that replaces primary tags.

functions.name: Withdraw or yank release
functions.description: Mark a published version withdrawn or yanked while retaining historical identity for exposure analysis.

functions.name: Issue advisory
functions.description: Publish a CSAF document with tracking identity, publisher authority, TLP and product tree.

functions.name: Disclose SBOM or inventory
functions.description: Share a catalogue, SBOM or operator inventory under TLP, contractual and access-scope rules, auditing disclosure separately from public product pages.

functions.name: Retire deployment
functions.description: Decommission a deployed system and remove corresponding primary, patch and supplemental tags per the SWID/CoSWID lifecycle.

composition.purpose: Product releases are composed of components and packages whose own identity, ecosystem metadata and internal files are modelled there. This model holds the composition relation, the declared constraint and the recorded resolution; it does not restate component internals.

Producer, supplier, SBOM author, advisory publisher and deployment operator are all party references. Candidate sibling, not confirmed in the registry relations; recorded as a reference obligation rather than an assumed link.

Copyright holders, relicensing authority and the underlying rights instruments behind a licence expression live outside this model; only the expression, its determination basis and a holder reference are held here.

Governance of purl types, the CPE dictionary and tag-issuer rules belongs to the identifier model; this model records which coordinates denote the product and how scheme conflicts are resolved per use.

Datasets consumed or produced by the software, including training data for AI-enabled products, are referenced rather than described. SPDX carries a separate Dataset profile for exactly this separation.

composition.target: Vulnerability record model (CVE Program record format)
composition.purpose: Vulnerability records, weakness classifications and scoring vectors are governed externally; this model references the identifier and holds only the product's exposure and exploitability judgement.

Where the product is AI-enabled, model cards, training provenance and model-specific evaluation extend this model rather than duplicating into it; both SPDX and CycloneDX treat this as a separate profile or object.

Alignment for element identity, artifact and package structure, relationships, creation information, integrity methods, external identifiers and the Software, Security, Licensing and Build profiles. Alignment only; no conformance is claimed without a cited conformance artifact.

Alignment for BOM metadata, component typing, services, dependency graph, compositions, lifecycle phases, formulation and declarations. Component-versus-package granularity differs from SPDX and is recorded as a conflict rather than harmonised silently.
Alignment for the governed global coordinate used to identify the distributed form of a release across ecosystems; purl is a coordinate, never the master key.

composition.target: OASIS CSAF v2.0 including the VEX profile
composition.purpose: Alignment for advisory tracking, product trees with identification helpers, product status vocabularies, remediations, scores and threats used by the advisory and exploitability findings.

Alignment for life cycle stage vocabulary (acquisition, supply, development, operation, maintenance, disposal) and for the product quality characteristics used to specify and measure quality. Full texts are paywalled, so alignment is at catalogue-scope level and flagged as an evidence gap.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Claude's aggregate framing is accepted over grok's entity framing. Release records, bill-of-materials documents, advisories, deployed-instance records and configuration snapshots each have their own lifecycle, their own authoring party and their own retention duty, yet none is meaningful except anchored to one product identity. Grok's own structure carries the same independently-lifecycled children (publication event logs, CSAF documents, operator inventory records, endpoint evidence) while labelling the root an entity, which understates the ownership split it itself enforces between producer catalogue and operator inventory. Aggregate is therefore the honest boundary, and the producer-side / operator-side seam is the aggregate's internal ownership line rather than a second model.

decisions.concept: Base provider selection
decisions.rationale: Claude carries seven boundary notes each with a named neighbour, a stated distinction and source refs, plus explicit in-scope and out-of-scope lists that survive adversarial testing (purl/CPE disagreement, producer acquisition, hosted-service-only delivery). Grok's boundaries are competent but push licensing, quality and regulatory conformity wholly out of scope, leaving a narrower object than the stated purpose requires. Size was not decisive; boundary completeness was.

decisions.concept: Entry kind
decisions.rationale: Releases, BOM documents, advisories and deployed-instance records have independent lifecycles and separate authoring parties, but are only interpretable anchored to one product identity. Grok's entity label contradicts the producer/operator ownership split grok itself enforces.

decisions.concept: Regulatory conformity (EU CRA and technical documentation)
decisions.rationale: Grok explicitly excludes CRA conformity dossiers and notified-body certificates; Claude models the regime, conformity route, declaration binding to a specific release, and documentation retention with legislative backing. Excluding it would remove the only structure connecting a release to the duty that keeps it lawfully on a market. Retained with the base's own caveat that non-EU regimes are placeholders.

decisions.concept: Rights and licensing bundle
decisions.disposition: Retained in scope from base as obligations-and-references, not licence mastering
decisions.rationale: Grok delegates licensing entirely to an IP sibling. The base's narrower reading is correct and is kept: licence expression, declared-versus-concluded basis, attribution and reciprocal reach, corresponding-source duration, and use and export restrictions are product-level obligations, while licence instruments, texts and disputes stay in the sibling model.

decisions.concept: Quality characteristics and verification evidence
decisions.rationale: Grok has no analogue. The base binds quality measures to a governed quality model and binds verification results to artifact digests rather than version strings, which is the only place in either provider where evidence is tied to the exact bytes tested. Kept, with the paywalled-standard evidence limitation carried as a hold.

decisions.concept: Family, edition, channel and SKU
decisions.rationale: Closes a gap the base explicitly declares as a known omission, with CoSWID software-meta and CSAF product-tree backing. Without it, editions of one code base must be modelled as unrelated products or collapsed into versions, and both are wrong.

decisions.concept: SWID/CoSWID tag types and patch-versus-upgrade
decisions.rationale: Neither RFC 9393 nor NISTIR 8060 was consulted by the base, and no base finding distinguishes corpus, primary, patch and supplemental identification records or the patch-must-not-change-version rule. This is grok's strongest unique evidence axis and it lands cleanly on an existing base layer.

decisions.concept: Composition completeness aggregates and coverage
decisions.rationale: The base has declared depth and known unknowns but no governed completeness vocabulary; CycloneDX compositions supply one that makes composition-evidence quality measurable rather than narrated. Accepted on the CycloneDX grounding alone; the CISA element-rename claim is held for field-level verification.

decisions.concept: Advisory remediation, restart and fix entitlement
decisions.rationale: The base can say a product is affected but cannot say what fix exists, whether applying it requires a restart, or who is entitled to obtain it. CSAF remediations carry exactly these fields, and the fix-access gate is distinct from the product-acquisition entitlement already modelled under restrictions.

decisions.concept: SBOM authorship, type and generation context
decisions.disposition: Rejected as a finding; sbomType taxonomy deferred to element enrichment
decisions.rationale: Two of its three questions duplicate the base's bill-of-materials-document (author identity versus producer, document creation time versus release time). Only the sbomType axis (design, source, build, analyzed, deployed, runtime) is genuinely new, which is one element's worth of value and does not justify a parallel finding beside an existing one.

decisions.concept: Producer, creator, supplier and maintainer roles
decisions.rationale: The base's producer-and-stewardship already asks which role owns each slice, who may publish binding statements, whether record author differs from producer, and what happens on succession. Grok's CoSWID role vocabulary and reg-id naming authority are element-level refinements of that finding, not a separate decision surface.

decisions.concept: Contained components and declared dependencies
decisions.rationale: The base's dependency-graph-and-resolution already holds declared constraint, scope, optionality, build-time resolution and pinning. Importing grok's component-grain containment finding would thicken the COMPOSE seam to WM-SFT-007 that both providers agree must stay thin.

decisions.concept: Product status and VEX assertions
decisions.rationale: Fully covered by the base's exploitability-assessment, which additionally models applicability conditions and retention of superseded assessments. Only grok's CSAF mandatory-test rule on contradicting product status is new, and that is a validation rule rather than structure.

decisions.concept: Publication, withdrawal and yank as a finding
decisions.disposition: Rejected as a finding; accepted as the withdraw-release function
decisions.rationale: The base's release-record already carries pre-release, generally available, superseded, withdrawn and yanked states plus the withdrawal event and its replacement. The gap was operational, not structural, so it is closed by adding the function rather than a duplicate finding.

decisions.concept: Hosting environment and discovery evidence
decisions.disposition: Rejected as duplicative; endpoint-digest matching deferred
decisions.rationale: Grok bundles genuinely new discovery-evidence content (payload versus on-device evidence, observed hash compared against the published digest set) with hosting-environment content that closely matches the base finding at high similarity. Importing the whole would duplicate; the new part is recorded as deferred element enrichment of deployed-instance-record.

decisions.concept: Service and hosted-offering treatment
decisions.disposition: Merged into base deployment and interface layers
decisions.rationale: Both providers treat services as within the product's runtime trust boundary rather than a separate model: the base records external services and data flows under runtime-configuration-and-interfaces and degrades release and integrity findings explicitly for SaaS-only delivery. No separate service layer is created; grok's service-boundary question is absorbed there.

decisions.concept: SBOM format harmonisation
decisions.disposition: Refused; per-document format and specification version retained
decisions.rationale: SPDX and CycloneDX draw the component boundary differently and both providers recognise this. The base's rule of storing source format and spec version per document is kept rather than harmonising into one shape, which also lets the CycloneDX 1.6 versus 1.7 pin be resolved later without restructuring.

publicationHolds: Source and live-version verification for every accepted source before publication: the providers disagree on SPDX 3.0.1 publisher attribution (Linux Foundation alone versus Linux Foundation with OMG), on the CycloneDX pin (1.6 with ECMA-424 June 2024 versus 1.7 with ECMA-424 December 2025), and on the ECMA-427 PURL edition; SLSA v1.1 is recorded as retired in favour of v1.2. Each URL must be re-fetched and each pin restated before any alignment claim is published.

Field-level verification of the 2026 CISA minimum elements against the source PDF tables. The providers give divergent readings of the same document: the base speaks of declared depth and adds component hash and licence, while the source provider claims Depth is replaced by Coverage and Supplier Name by Component Producer, and itself admits the PDF body was not fully field-extracted. No element name from this document may be bound in the published draft until the tables are read directly.

Multi-domain profile validation across at least five delivery profiles before the coverage claim stands: commercial on-premises application, open-source library in a package ecosystem, container image, firmware-as-software, and SaaS-only offering with no distributable artifact. The base states that release and integrity findings degrade for the SaaS case; that degradation must be exercised rather than asserted.

Clause-level confirmation of ISO/IEC 19770-2:2015 and NISTIR 8060 for the accepted tag-type finding, since the source provider states the 19770-2 XML schema annexes were not retrieved in full and the tag information model was carried via RFC 9393 and paraphrase.

Paywalled-standard limitation must be restated at publication: alignment to ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207:2026 and ISO/IEC 25010:2023 rests on catalogue-level scope statements, not clause-level reading, and no conformance to SPDX, CycloneDX, CSAF, ISO 19770-2 or 12207 is claimed.
deferredResearch: SBOM type taxonomy (design, source, build, analyzed, deployed, runtime) plus tool name and version and generation context, to be absorbed as elements of the existing bill-of-materials-document finding rather than a parallel finding, once the CISA element names are verified against the PDF tables.

Advisory TLP labelling, sharing constraints, CSAF document status lifecycle (draft, interim, final, withdrawn) and profile selection, as element enrichment of advisory-and-exposure-mapping and of the model's access policy rather than as a separate advisory-identity finding.

Endpoint discovery evidence: CoSWID payload versus on-device evidence mutual exclusivity, and comparison of observed endpoint file or image hashes against the published release digest set, as element enrichment of deployed-instance-record.

Accessibility conformance, which the base names as a live structural gap with no authoritative source consulted; treating it as a quality subcharacteristic is probably insufficient for products subject to accessibility legislation.
Cryptographic bill of materials and cryptographic asset inventory for post-quantum migration planning, currently reachable only through a component-type reference.
AI-specific and SaaS-specific extra transparency elements, including the separately published CISA AI SBOM minimum elements, which both providers flag as required extras but neither expands.

CoSWID entity role vocabulary (aggregator, distributor, licensor, maintainer) with reg-id naming authority, as elements on producer-and-stewardship so role assertions can be correlated across documents.
SPDX 3.1 release-candidate expansion into hardware, safety and operations, tracked as emerging and deliberately excluded from the canonical structure until it is formally published.

Product-line variability beyond edition and channel (feature flags, software product lines) and per-jurisdiction export-control classification schemes, neither of which has primary support in either provider run.

model.name: Software Component / Package
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to identify, classify, verify, compose, govern and operate a versioned, distributable software component or package release used as a dependency.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the identifiable software component or package as a distributable unit: its project-level and release-level identity, version designation, contained and depended-upon composition, origin and build provenance, licensing and regulatory obligations, lifecycle state, vulnerability exposure, distribution channel and the provenance of every assertion made about it. It deliberately stops at the boundary of the consuming product, the SBOM document, the advisory record and the running deployment, each of which is a sibling or parent model. Storage and interface (JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MCP, MongoDB) are projections of this model, never its semantics.
in_scope: Project-level identity (ecosystem type, namespace, name) and release-level identity (version, distribution variants, content digests).
Cross-scheme identifier alignment: purl, CPE, SWID, content identifiers, OCI descriptors and registry-native keys.
Declared dependency constraints, resolved dependency closures, contained files, bundled subcomponents and pedigree or derivation.
Origin and supply-chain provenance: supplier, author, manufacturer and distributor roles, source revision linkage, build attestation and signature verification.
Declared and concluded licensing, attribution and notice obligations attaching to redistribution.
Release lifecycle state (pre-release, published, deprecated, yanked, withdrawn, removed), support window and replacement path.
Vulnerability affectedness of a specific version, exploitability status, remediation decisions and time-bounded exceptions.
Distribution channel, registry of record, retrieval location, availability, unpublish and retention behaviour.
Assertion-level provenance: who asserted a fact, from which source, with what evidence and confidence, at which event and observation time.
out_of_scope: The composed software product or service that consumes the component, and its architecture (WM-SFT-001).
The SBOM document itself, its structure, exchange, signing and distribution (WM-SFT-012); only the reference edge and coverage claims remain here.
Vulnerability and advisory records as first-class entities (CVE, GHSA, OSV entries); only the affectedness edge for a version is in scope.
Source repository, branch and commit management, code review and contribution process.
Build platform, pipeline and runner configuration as entities; only the emitted provenance predicate and its subject digest are referenced.
Deployed or running instances, hosts, containers at runtime and operational telemetry.
Legal-entity master data for suppliers, maintainers and stewards; only the role edge is in scope.
Licence texts, licence drafting and legal interpretation; only the expression and derived obligations are in scope.
Cryptographic key material, trust roots, key issuance and rotation procedures.
Hardware bills of material and non-software components.

boundary_notes.distinction: A product or service is the marketed and operated whole; a package is a versioned distributable unit reusable across many products. SPDX models both as Package instances distinguished only by purpose vocabularies, so the distinction must be carried by the composition edge, not by the class.

An SBOM is a document asserting a component set at a point in time; SPDX models it as a distinct Sbom class. The component exists independently of any SBOM, so SBOM structure, completeness and exchange belong to the sibling model.

The OSV entry is the authority-published record with its own identifier, aliases, ranges and modification time. This model stores only the resolved verdict for a concrete version plus the evidence of that resolution.
SLSA provenance describes the build run, its builder identity and parameters. The package holds the subject digest and the attestation reference; the run itself is a separate event entity.

purl types such as github and golang can address version-control locations, but a revision is not a distributable release with its own distribution artifacts and lifecycle state; the two must not be conflated.

CPE names classes of IT products for platform enumeration and vulnerability matching; it does not address a specific downloadable artifact. purl does. Mapping between them is lossy and must be recorded as an alignment.
SWID tags describe software installed on an endpoint, including patch and supplemental tags for asset management. Endpoint installation state is asset data, not package identity.
An OCI image is addressed by a content descriptor digest and may also carry a purl of type oci. It extends package identity with layered content addressing rather than replacing it.

findings.name: Ecosystem coordinate identity
findings.description: The purl type, optional namespace and name that address the component in its ecosystem of record, plus the normalization rules that must run before any comparison.

data_elements.name: Canonical purl
data_elements.description: Normalized Package URL string for the component, versionless at project level and versioned at release level.

data_elements.name: Package type
data_elements.description: purl type token identifying the ecosystem or packaging convention, lowercase ASCII and never starting with a digit.

data_elements.name: Package namespace
data_elements.description: Type-specific grouping prefix such as a Maven groupId, npm scope or Go module path prefix.

data_elements.name: Package name
data_elements.description: Registry-native name of the component within its type and namespace.

findings.name: Cross-scheme identifier alignment
findings.description: Additional identifier schemes asserted for the component (CPE, SWID, content identifiers such as SWHID or OmniBOR) and the confidence and directionality of each mapping.

data_elements.name: CPE name
data_elements.description: Common Platform Enumeration name asserted for the product class corresponding to this component.

data_elements.name: SWID tag identifier
data_elements.description: ISO/IEC 19770-2 software identification tag identifier associated with the installed form of this component.

data_elements.name: Content identifier
data_elements.description: Content-derived identifier such as a Software Heritage identifier or OmniBOR artifact identifier.

data_elements.name: Identifier mapping confidence
data_elements.description: Recorded confidence class for a cross-scheme identifier assertion.

findings.name: Content address and integrity verification
findings.description: Cryptographic digests over the exact released byte streams, the algorithms accepted, and the mandatory verification step before consumption.

data_elements.name: Artifact digest
data_elements.description: Digest of a released artifact in algorithm:encoded form, acting as the content identifier and comparison key.

data_elements.name: Artifact size
data_elements.description: Size in bytes of the raw content addressed by the digest.

data_elements.name: Integrity verification outcome
data_elements.description: Result of verifying retrieved bytes against the recorded digest, together with the verifying actor.

data_elements.name: Verification time
data_elements.description: Observation time at which integrity verification was executed.

findings.name: Version scheme, precedence and immutability
findings.description: Which versioning scheme governs the version string, how two versions are ordered, and whether published content for a version is immutable.

data_elements.name: Version string
data_elements.description: Opaque version token as published by the registry of record, stored verbatim before any interpretation.

data_elements.name: Version scheme
data_elements.description: Identifier of the ordering scheme that applies to the version string, such as a semantic, ecosystem-specific or opaque scheme.

data_elements.name: Version precedence key
data_elements.description: Derived sortable key computed by the declared scheme's precedence function, never used as an identifier.

data_elements.name: Pre-release indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the version designates a pre-release that ranks below the corresponding normal version.

findings.name: Release variant and distribution set
findings.description: The distinct distribution artifacts that constitute one release (source distribution, binaries, platform and architecture variants) and how a consumer selects among them.

data_elements.name: Distribution artifact
data_elements.description: One downloadable file belonging to the release, with file name, media type, digest and qualifiers.

data_elements.name: Target platform qualifier
data_elements.description: Operating system, architecture or runtime qualifier constraining where an artifact is usable.

data_elements.name: Primary purpose
data_elements.description: Classification of what the artifact is, such as library, application, container, firmware, source or data.

findings.name: Component type and software purpose
findings.description: CycloneDX requires a component type such as application, library, framework, container, operating-system, firmware, file or machine-learning-model. SPDX records primaryPurpose and additionalPurpose, noting that purpose is intrinsic to how the element is used rather than solely to its content. The two vocabularies overlap but are not identical.

data_elements.name: CycloneDX component type
data_elements.description: Required type in CycloneDX component records.

data_elements.name: SPDX primary purpose
data_elements.description: Primary SoftwarePurpose of the package.

data_elements.name: SPDX additional purposes
data_elements.description: Additional SoftwarePurpose values.

findings.name: Declared dependency constraints
findings.description: The dependency edges the component itself declares, with version constraint expressions, scope and linkage kind.

data_elements.name: Declared dependency edge
data_elements.description: One declared relationship from this component to a target coordinate, with its constraint and scope.

data_elements.name: Version constraint expression
data_elements.description: The version range or pin as declared, retained verbatim alongside its interpretation scheme.

data_elements.name: Dependency scope
data_elements.description: Scope classification of the dependency, such as required, optional or excluded.

data_elements.name: Linkage kind
data_elements.description: How the dependency is bound at build or run time: static, dynamic or tool-only.

findings.name: Resolved dependency closure
findings.description: The concrete transitive set a resolver selected at a stated instant, together with the completeness of that closure.

data_elements.name: Resolved component reference
data_elements.description: A concrete component release selected by the resolver, identified by versioned purl and where available by digest.

data_elements.name: Resolution timestamp
data_elements.description: Event time at which the resolver produced the closure.

data_elements.name: Closure completeness
data_elements.description: Declared completeness of the closure, including whether unknown areas are asserted rather than silently omitted.

findings.name: Contained files, snippets and bundled subcomponents
findings.description: Files and subpaths inside the released artifact, and third-party code bundled or vendored without a manifest declaration.

data_elements.name: Contained file entry
data_elements.description: One file inside the artifact with its kind, path and content identifier.

data_elements.name: Bundled subcomponent
data_elements.description: A nested component detected inside the artifact that is not a declared dependency.

data_elements.name: Normalized subpath
data_elements.description: Relative path within the package, normalized by stripping leading and trailing separators and dot segments.

findings.name: Pedigree, patches and derivation
findings.description: Ancestry of the component: what it was derived from, what modifications were applied, and how confident that chain is.

data_elements.name: Ancestor reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the component or revision this component was derived from.

data_elements.name: Applied modification
data_elements.description: A patch, commit or configuration change applied on top of the ancestor.

data_elements.name: Derivation kind
data_elements.description: Classification of how this component relates to its ancestor, such as fork, rebuild, repackage or verbatim redistribution.

findings.name: Supplier, author and distributor roles
findings.description: The distinct agents who originated, supplied and distributed the release, and which of those is accountable for security response.

data_elements.name: Supplying agent
data_elements.description: Agent that supplied the component release to the consumer, distinct from the originating author.

data_elements.name: Originating agent
data_elements.description: Agent that authored or manufactured the component.

data_elements.name: Role assertion basis
data_elements.description: How each role claim was established: self-declared metadata, contractual record, or verified attestation.

data_elements.name: Steward status
data_elements.description: Whether an open-source steward or equivalent non-commercial maintainer stands behind the component.

findings.name: Source revision and repository linkage
findings.description: The repository and exact revision corresponding to the release, and what if anything verifies that link beyond a self-declared URL.

data_elements.name: Version control URL
data_elements.description: Location of the source repository associated with the component.

data_elements.name: Source revision identifier
data_elements.description: Exact revision, such as a commit digest, claimed to correspond to the release.

data_elements.name: Source link verification status
data_elements.description: Whether the artifact-to-revision link is unverified, attested or independently reproduced.

findings.name: Build provenance attestation
findings.description: The provenance predicate binding the artifact digest to a build platform, build type, parameters and time window, and the assurance level claimed from it.

data_elements.name: Build type URI
data_elements.description: Type URI identifying the template for how the build was performed and how its parameters are interpreted.

data_elements.name: Builder identifier
data_elements.description: Type URI identifying the transitive closure of the trusted build platform.

data_elements.name: Build start instant
data_elements.description: Event time at which the build run began, as reported by the build platform.

data_elements.name: Build finish instant
data_elements.description: Event time at which the build run completed.

data_elements.name: Provenance level claim
data_elements.description: Assurance level asserted for the build provenance, together with the assessing party.

findings.name: Signature, envelope and admission decision
findings.description: Signature and attestation envelopes covering the artifact, the verification policy that gates admission, and how exceptions are authorised.

data_elements.name: Signature or envelope reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a signed envelope covering an attestation or artifact for this release.

data_elements.name: Signer identity
data_elements.description: Identity asserted by the signing material, resolved to an agent where possible.

data_elements.name: Verification policy identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the admission policy applied to this component.

findings.name: Declared and concluded licensing
findings.description: The licence expression the supplier declares, the expression a reviewer concludes, and how ambiguity and choice under disjunction are recorded.

data_elements.name: Declared licence expression
data_elements.description: Licence expression as declared by the supplier, canonicalized to SPDX expression syntax where parseable.

data_elements.name: Concluded licence expression
data_elements.description: Licence expression concluded by review, which may differ from the declaration.

data_elements.name: Recorded licence choice
data_elements.description: The disjunct selected by the adopting Dimension when the expression offers a choice.

data_elements.name: Licence determining agent
data_elements.description: Agent accountable for the concluded licence determination.

findings.name: Attribution, notice and redistribution obligations
findings.description: The concrete obligations triggered by redistributing the component and the evidence that they were met.

data_elements.name: Copyright text
data_elements.description: Copyright statement associated with the component or its contained files.

data_elements.name: Attribution text
data_elements.description: Text that must be reproduced when redistributing the component.

data_elements.name: Obligation item
data_elements.description: A single derived obligation with its trigger, owner and fulfilment state.

findings.name: Support period and third-party due diligence
findings.description: The support period determined for products containing the component and the due-diligence step required before integrating a third-party or open-source component.

data_elements.name: Support period end date
data_elements.description: Date until which vulnerabilities in products containing this component will be handled by the responsible manufacturer.

data_elements.name: Applicable regulation
data_elements.description: Regulatory instrument asserted to apply to the component in a given market.

data_elements.name: Due-diligence record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the completed due-diligence assessment for this component.

findings.name: Component disclosure and incident reporting duties
findings.description: What component data must be disclosed to customers or authorities, to whom, in what form, and on what deadlines once a vulnerability is actively exploited.

data_elements.name: Disclosure obligation
data_elements.description: A required disclosure with its recipient, form and legal basis.

data_elements.name: Reporting deadline
data_elements.description: Elapsed-time deadline measured from the triggering event for a required notification.

data_elements.name: Redaction basis
data_elements.description: Recorded justification for withholding component detail from a disclosure.

findings.name: Release state and transitions
findings.description: The current published state of the release, the transitions permitted, and how a resolver must behave in each state.
